newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Senate defeat budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Senate defeat budget amendment.

text.p: President Clinton urged the Senate to defeat a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution, saying in a letter to Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle that it would "pose grave risks to the Social Security system."
In addition, he asserted it would lock the government into a form of budgeting that might not be appropriate during an economic slowdown or recession.
Clinton reiterated his pledge to balance the budget. "This commitment notwithstanding, I am convinced that we should not have a balanced budget amendment."
"I believe that a historic budget agreement that achieves balance by 2002 is within reach this year," Clinton said in the letter.
Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget to be released February 6 will detail his proposed path for the government to reach balance by 2002.

Senate Republicans have said they expect a vote will occur by the end of February. While it was defeated in the Senate last year by only one vote, Daschle said sufficient numbers of Democrats were leaning to vote for it to permit passage. To pass, 67 votes are needed and all 55 Republicans have signed on as co-sponsors.
The amendment would require the budget be balanced in peacetime and would make it difficult for Congress to approve deficit spending, new taxes or an increase in government borrowing.
The House is also expected to vote by the end of February and Republicans say they face an uphill fight for passage. It passed the House last year when Republicans held a larger majority.
